Reporting to the Chief Data Officer, the role turns strategy into reliable platforms, pipelines, APIs and AI/ML infrastructure used by clinical, research and operational teams. This is a hands-on leadership role in NHG’s data and AI transformation. The Director leads engineering delivery, architecture and standards, builds a multi-disciplinary team, and works with CDO, IT, analytics and clinical stakeholders to ensure NHG’s data infrastructure is secure, reliable, interoperable and scalable. The role is accountable for technology delivery and for the clinical, operational and business outcomes enabled by data and AI engineering. Scope and Interfaces Reports to the Chief Data Officer and leads the engineering function within the Data and AI Office. Owns engineering delivery, technical architecture, engineering standards, platform production readiness and engineering assurance for data and AI products, ensuring alignment with NHG Health’s technology partners, MOH requirements, and Singapore’s national data engineering strategy and digital health initiatives. Partners with the CDO to ensure the engineering roadmap is directly tied to measurable clinical, operational, research and population health outcomes, and that engineering investment decisions are communicated in terms of business value to senior stakeholders. Partners with IT, cybersecurity, enterprise architecture, infrastructure and procurement teams on hosting, cloud, network, identity, security, resilience and enterprise technology standards. Works with data governance, clinical informatics, responsible AI, privacy and compliance teams to translate policy requirements into technical controls. Collaborates with clinical, operational, research, population health and corporate stakeholders to convert use cases into scalable engineering solutions. Key Responsibilities 1. Lead design of NHG data strategy and its translation into engineering delivery Design and execute NHG’s data and AI strategy into a clear engineering roadmap, delivery plan and prioritised backlog aligned to clinical, operational, research and population health goals. 2. Build and run data and AI platforms Design, build and operate secure, scalable platforms, pipelines, APIs and AI/ML infrastructure that support trusted data use across NHG with DataOps/MLOPs/AIOps capabilities. 3. Ensure reliability and production readiness Set standards for performance, uptime, monitoring, incident response, documentation and continuous improvement of production data and AI service, with day 2 monitoring for AI capabilities. 4. Embed security, privacy and responsible AI Translate governance, data protection, HIM and responsible AI requirements into practical engineering controls, audit evidence and safe operating practices. 5. Lead and grow the engineering team Recruit, develop and lead a multi-disciplinary engineering team with strong technical discipline, delivery accountability, continuous learning and future skill proofing. 6. Manage technology and vendor choices Evaluate tools, platforms, vendors and build-versus-buy options based on scalability, interoperability, security, cost, supportability and alignment with national technology initiatives in collaboration with health tech agencies. 7. Partner across NHG and national initiatives Work with CDO, IT, cybersecurity, governance, analytics, clinical, corporate and national stakeholders to translate needs into practical engineering solutions and communicate progress, risks and value clearly. Overview of Key Results Areas The role will be assessed against key results areas that show how data and AI engineering enables NHG’s clinical, operational, research and population health priorities. Platform delivery: Secure, scalable and reusable data and AI platforms aligned with NHG and national priorities. Production readiness: Priority data products and AI solutions safely moved into monitored, sustainable use. Governance-by-design: Security, privacy, data governance, HIM and responsible AI built into engineering practices. Capability building: Strong engineering team with mature DevOps, DataOps, MLOps and production support practices. Value and impact: Reduced duplication, trusted data products, faster delivery and measurable clinical, operational and research value, and user satisfactions. Key Requirements Essential At least 12 years of experience in software engineering, data engineering, platform engineering or related technology leadership roles. At least 5 years leading multi-disciplinary engineering teams in complex enterprise environments. Strong technical depth in data engineering, cloud infrastructure, API design, integration architecture, modern software engineering and production operations. Proven experience delivering enterprise-grade platforms or digital systems with strong reliability, security, supportability and governance expectations. Experience with DevOps, DataOps, ALOps and or MLOps practices, including CI/CD, automated testing, monitoring, observability and infrastructure-as-code. Demonstrated ability to communicate engineering strategy, technical trade-offs and delivery risks in business and clinical terms to senior non-technical stakeholders. Experience managing engineering cost transparency, total cost of ownership and value-for-money reporting. Ability to communicate technical trade-offs, delivery risks, value and implementation options clearly to clinical, operational, governance and executive stakeholders. Preferred Healthcare, public-sector or other regulated-industry technology experience. Experience with AI/ML platforms, MLOps, LLM-enabled solutions, generative AI or agentic AI in production settings. Familiarity with healthcare interoperability, clinical safety, data governance, data protection and HIM-related requirements. Experience managing vendors, technology partners, build-vs-buy decisions and value-for-money assessments in enterprise settings. Familiarity with Singapore's national technology landscape, including GovTech platforms, MOH digital health initiatives or whole-of-government cloud and data infrastructure. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field; a Master's degree is an advantage. The role is responsible for shaping NUH’s global capability-building strategy, scaling internationally relevant programmes, strengthening institutional alliances, and ensuring disciplined governance, financial sustainability and reputational stewardship across all global engagements. Key Responsibilities: 1. Strategic Leadership & Portfolio Integration Set the strategic direction and multi-year roadmap for NUH’s Global Academy, Consultancy, Alliances and Mission portfolios, aligned with NUH’s overall internationalisation and academic health system strategy. Ensure coherence and synergy across education, advisory, partnership and mission activities to maximise institutional impact and resource efficiency. Translate NUH clinical, academic and operational strengths into scalable global offerings relevant to international health systems. 2. Global Academy (Education & Capability Development) Provide oversight of healthcare management education, leadership development and training programmes delivered to international partners under the Global Academy. Ensure programmes are academically robust, operationally viable and aligned with NUH’s brand and values. Expand fellowship, exchange and leadership platforms that position NUH as a regional centre for healthcare capability-building. 3. Global Consultancy (Advisory & Systems Transformation) Lead NUH’s Global Consultancy strategy, including market positioning, service portfolio development and quality assurance. Oversee delivery of consultancy engagements with overseas hospitals, health systems and ministries, ensuring outcomes-driven, ethically governed and financially sustainable projects. Ensure strong governance over contracting, fees, risk management and compliance with NUH/NUHS policies. 4. Strategic / Global Alliances Develop and steward strategic institutional alliances with international hospitals, universities, health authorities and multilateral partners. Oversee alliance frameworks, fellowship networks and collaborative platforms (e.g. academic, leadership, innovation or systems pilots). Ensure alliances deliver clear strategic value, reciprocity and long-term institutional benefit to NUH. 5. Global Mission & Outreach Provide leadership over NUH’s Global Mission initiatives, including community health missions, health system strengthening and capability transfer programmes in the region. Ensure missions are aligned with NUH’s values, clinical governance standards and reputation. Balance humanitarian objectives with sustainability, staff welfare and institutional priorities. 6. Governance, Risk & Institutional Stewardship Ensure all global education, consultancy and partnership activities comply with NUH/NUHS governance frameworks, including agreement review, fee management, conflict of interest and overseas travel policies. Act as a key institutional steward of NUH’s global reputation, managing sensitivities across jurisdictions, partners and stakeholders. Provide regular updates to senior management on portfolio performance, risks, opportunities and strategic issues. 7. Financial & Operational Accountability Oversee budgeting, revenue generation, cost control and financial sustainability of the global portfolios. Ensure appropriate resourcing, team capability development and staff welfare across the Global Academy, Consultancy, Alliances and Mission teams. 8. Stakeholder & Senior-Level Engagement Represent NUH in high-level engagements with international partners, government agencies, multilateral organisations and academic institutions. Support CEO and senior leadership in shaping NUH’s global narrative and positioning. Key Competencies & Experience: Essential Senior leadership experience in healthcare, academic medicine, health systems or international programmes. Proven track record in international partnerships, education, consultancy or system-wide initiatives. Strong strategic thinking with the ability to operationalise complex, multi-country initiatives. High governance acumen, particularly in risk, compliance and institutional reputational management. Desirable Experience working with overseas hospitals, ministries of health or multilateral partners. Familiarity with healthcare education, leadership development or management consultancy models. Exposure to global health, capacity-building or mission-oriented programmes. Personal Attributes Strategic, diplomatic and politically astute. Credible with senior clinicians, executives and external partners. Values-driven, with strong commitment to governance, professionalism and staff wellbeing. jobs.title: Deputy/Assistant Director, AI Capability Development (3-year Contract)
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 16 Sep 2026. Closing on 12 Oct 2026. Artificial intelligence is creating new opportunities to enhance productivity, strengthen risk management and enable new forms of financial services. To support the responsible adoption of AI across the financial sector, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) works with financial institutions, AI firms, FinTechs, technology providers, academia and public-sector partners to develop the capabilities, partnerships and enabling frameworks needed to translate advances in AI into meaningful industry outcomes. Within MAS, the Financial Infrastructure & Artificial Intelligence Office (FIA) leads initiatives that strengthen the foundations for AI innovation in financial services. This includes ecosystem development, strategic partnerships, data and digital infrastructure, industry capability building, and national-level initiatives that support the safe, trusted and effective use of AI across the financial sector. This role focuses on strengthening AI capabilities and adoption across Singapore's financial sector. You will work closely with financial institutions to understand how AI is being deployed, identify barriers to adoption, and shape MAS' strategies to address them. Acting as a bridge between industry and MAS, you will work across policy, supervisory and industry development functions to ensure that MAS' initiatives support the responsible adoption of AI. By bringing together industry insights, implementation experience and regulatory perspectives, you will help create the conditions for financial institutions to deploy AI safely, responsibly and at scale. Your responsibilities will include: Industry Capability Development: Shape strategies to strengthen AI capabilities and adoption across the financial sector Industry Engagement: Work closely with financial institutions and industry stakeholders to develop initiatives that support industry transformation Industry Enablement: Improve the enabling environment for responsible AI adoption Strategic Planning: Drive MAS' approach to supporting AI capability development and adoption across the financial sector Industry Insights: Monitor AI adoption trends, implementation experience and emerging challenges across the financial sector to inform MAS' strategies and initiatives At least 5 years of relevant experience in strategy, consulting, industry development, innovation, business transformation, public policy, regulation, supervision, compliance or risk management within financial services or the public sector Strong understanding of the opportunities and challenges associated with AI adoption within financial institutions. jobs.jd: Posting Date: 2 Oct 2026. Closing on 16 Oct 2026. [What the role is] 1. Oversee compilation, analysis and reporting of key tourism statistics, ensuring that communication of tourism performance outcomes and delivery of insights are done in a timely manner. 2. Translate data and research into actionable and meaningful insights that would guide both internal teams and external industry stakeholders, with the objective of driving data-driven decision making across the organisation. 3. Liaise and coordinate with information agencies across Whole-of-Government (WOG). 4. Fulfilment of analytics deliverables and where applicable, data partnerships with external stakeholders. [What you will be working on] 1. Lead, manage and drive data cleaning, exploration, ingestion, compilation and analysis to derive insights and support business outcomes related to STB’s key tourism performance measures including Visitor Arrivals, Tourism Receipts, Hotels Stats. 2. Direct and coordinate data collection and analytics strategies, analysis of data collected from both quantitative and qualitative methods to come up with evidence-based insights that will help drive business outcomes. This includes performing data wrangling and transformation to prepare raw data into analysis-ready formats, manage data ingestion, applying statistical/analytical methods to extract insights from data, utilising data visualisation tools to communicate findings effectively. 3. Deliver tourism performance insights to stakeholders. 4. Monitor and lead a team on regular reporting, publications and data requests from stakeholders and maintain key databases from which analysis is drawn from. 5. Oversee all aspects of project management, ranging from contract and vendor management to end-to-end data operations, including fulfilling data custodian role of ensuring good quality data, developing and/or enhancing existing datasets and dashboards. 6. Collaborate with cross-functional teams, such as product managers, data scientists/engineers and business stakeholders, to integrate and deploy models and dashboards into analytics platforms. 7. Provide data advisory support to internal (within STB) and external (WOG, industry) stakeholders as relevant. This may include the assessment of economic contributions from major tourism projects. 8. Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to gather intelligence on emerging issues and provide actionable insights. 9. Provide effective leadership and guidance to the analytics team in the areas of operational data analytics including data manipulation to extract insights, synthesis of results and ensuring data accuracy and alignment with organisational outcomes and communicating the findings to stakeholders. 10. Grow a high-performance analytics team. [What we are looking for] a) Trained in Data Analytics, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Economics or a related quantitative discipline b) A minimum of 8 years of relevant experience in data analytics, interpretation and visualisation, with at least 3 years’ experience in leading teams. c) Strong foundational knowledge of data analytics methodologies and analytics skills, with a good eye for detail and possess an aptitude/experience in solving analytical problems using quantitative approaches. d) Good mastery of market research methodologies. e) Advantageous if you have experience in research applications in a client-side context. f) Working knowledge in statistical modelling and forecasting. g) Proven track record and hands on experience in integrating and synthesising research and data across multiple sources to derive meaningful conclusions. h) Proven track record in engaging different groups of stakeholders (within and outside of the organisation). i) Fluency in data manipulation to extract insights, strategic direction and narrative, forecasting and project future visitor demand. j) Strong business orientation with the ability to connect understanding from data to key business outcomes.

jobs.title: Assistant Director (Tech Strategy)
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 2 Oct 2026. Closing on 15 Oct 2026. Singapore is internationally renowned for our transport infrastructure and for being a global aviation and maritime hub. At the Ministry of Transport (MOT), we spearhead developments in our air, land and sea transport sectors to advance Singapore’s economic competitiveness and Singaporeans’ quality of life. We seek dynamic, analytical and committed individuals to join our able MOT team in realising our vision of a global interconnected transport hub. If you share our vision and possess the qualities we seek, do join us! As Assistant Director of Technology Strategy (AD-Tech Strat) in the Technology and Data Policy Department, you will be supporting the Deputy Director to advance Singapore’s transport and connectivity agenda through science, technology, and data innovation. You will contribute to policy development, strategic planning, and cross-agency coordination, while managing programmes that address emerging technological trends, and opportunities and risks. Key responsibilities include: 1. Policy Development & Strategic Planning • Formulate science and technology (S&T) and data policies aligned with national transport and connectivity goals. • Draft components of the MOT Family S&T Frameworks, programmes and plans, including supporting MOT's R&D agenda. • Plan and conduct workshops using futures thinking and horizon scanning methodologies to identify emerging issues, opportunities and risks. 2. Technology Evaluation & Risk Analysis • Monitor and assess emerging technologies (e.g., AI, cybersecurity, digital infrastructure) and their relevance to the transport sector. • Contribute to risk assessments and help identify regulatory gaps or strategic vulnerabilities concerning new scientific and technological advancements. 3. Stakeholder Engagement & Coordination • Liaise with other MOT HQ divisions, and Statutory Boards (SBs) to engage external partners like research institutions and industry ecosystem players to gather inputs and align policy directions. • Coordinate working groups and inter-agency meetings to support collaborative initiatives. 4. Capability Building & Transformation • Assist in implementing capability development programmes to enhance S&T planning and portfolio management, and data literacy across the MOT family. • Support transformation efforts in the SBs harness S&T and data effectively. Qualifications • Tertiary qualification in engineering, science and technology, public policy or other relevant fields. • Postgraduate qualification is an advantage Experience & Technical Skills • 3 years’ experience in public policy, S&T strategy, or data governance • Strong analytical and writing skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information. • Familiarity with futures thinking, innovation ecosystems, and public sector transformation. • Knowledge in public infrastructure, transport and engineering sector. Core Competencies • Strong communication (written & verbal), stakeholder management, and cross agency coordination skills. • Ability to manage multi stakeholder programmes with tight deadlines. • Sound judgement, attention to detail, and high standards of governance.

jobs.jd: Posting Date: 2 Oct 2026. Closing on 14 Oct 2026. jobs.jd: Posting Date: 1 Sep 2026. Closing on 17 Oct 2026. Who we are The Legal Policy Group (LPG) in the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) plays a critical role in upholding the rule of law, advancing access to justice, and ensuring a sound and progressive legal framework for Singaporeans. What the role is Under LPG, officers at the Criminal Policy Division (CPD) do not just review laws — we play an important role in helping to shape the future of legal policy and governance in Singapore. Our team has driven reforms that keep Singaporeans safe by improving our criminal justice system. Some recent initiatives include: • Protecting the public from dangerous offenders: In 2024, CPD worked closely with MHA to introduce the Sentence for Enhanced Public Protection (SEPP) to better protect the public from dangerous offenders. The SEPP applies to offenders who commit serious offences like rape and culpable homicide, and who are assessed to pose a risk of committing similar offences in the future. Under the SEPP, such offenders will only be released from prison if they no longer pose a threat of serious harm to others. This regime came into effect in July 2026. • Promoting inclusive justice: CPD supports the ongoing work of the Inclusive Justice Taskforce, which comprises representatives from the public and private sector. The Taskforce aims to develop recommendations to promote just outcomes and better support persons with disabilities and mental health conditions in their interactions with the criminal justice system. • Promoting consistency and transparency in sentencing: CPD support the Sentencing Advisory Panel, an interagency group which formulates and published guidelines on matters relating to sentencing including, most recently, guidelines on the sentencing of scams-related offences. • Safeguarding the quality of expert evidence in criminal proceedings: Expert opinion such as psychiatric evidence plays an important role in criminal proceedings. In 2025, CPD introduced a framework to govern expert opinion, including setting up a Panel of Psychiatrists to strengthen the quality and objectivity of psychiatric expert evidence. • Enhancing the victim compensation regime: In 2024, CPD operationalised enhancements to the criminal compensation process to encourage the use of compensation orders in favour of victims, and to increase victim participation in the process. • Safeguarding the administration of justice and the rule of law: In 2024, CPD introduced the amendments to the Administration of Justice (Protection) Act to make clear that egregious cases of abuse of process, such as filing of fictitious claims for purposes of delaying criminal proceedings and persistently commencing manifestly groundless actions, will amount to contempt of court. We are a small, multidisciplinary team that values thoughtful debate, moves with gumption, and is unafraid of breaking the mould. Officers will have the space to challenge assumptions and propose new ideas. This role is ideal for someone who is passionate about making a difference, thrives on intellectual challenge, and enjoys working collaboratively in a dynamic environment — and who wants their work to have tangible, national-level impact. You will join us in a variety of ongoing and upcoming policy reviews and reforms for the policy areas set out below: • Contribute to legal reform: Work with fellow officers to review laws, propose reforms and pursue new initiatives, tackling both classic and frontier issues. If you ever wanted to rewrite the rulebook (legally, of course), this is your chance. • Drive change, turn ideas into reality: Turn complex policy challenges into tangible solutions that improve real lives — take legislation from idea to Parliament, collaborating with legislative drafters, experts, and stakeholders. Become the bridge between policy vision and practical reality. • Engage stakeholders: Work with stakeholders and partners to develop creative, practical solutions to issues of national sig

(iv) Overseeing Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) within METI. The officer will undertake the following key responsibilities: • Design, organise and run robust planning processes across the METI Firefly Family to identify our Strategic Priorities, foster organisation-wide alignment, and ensure disciplined follow through with well-defined implementation plans, including guiding divisions in the formulation of their respective work plans. • Drive the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) process within METI to proactively anticipate challenges and support informed decision making. • Support the development of agendas and organising frameworks for METI-Exco and senior management meetings and coordinate the implementation of agreed strategies across clusters. • Design and implement strategic resource allocation frameworks, principles and tools (e.g. resourcing principles, benchmarks, reporting and evaluation mechanisms), to support the prudent and strategic allocation of budget and manpower resources across the METI family. • Work closely with stakeholders to understand resource requirements and priorities, balance competing demands, and uplift resource management capabilities within METI and the Firefly Family (e.g. conducting robust Cost-Benefit-Analysis). • Support the work of key Ministerial-level economic strategy decision making platforms and related work-streams. You should consider applying for this role if you: • Are keen to gain a high-level, whole-of-government perspective on Singapore’s economic goals and challenges, and to understand the strategic, policy and resourcing trade-offs underlying key economic decisions. • Are interested in broad-based exposure to core competencies such as corporate planning, strategic resource management, and stakeholder management and engagement. jobs.title: Senior Exec/Asst Dir/Senior Asst Director, Civil & Legislative Policy Division
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 29 Sep 2026. Closing on 17 Oct 2026. Who we are The Legal Policy Group (LPG) in the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) plays a critical role in upholding the rule of law, advancing access to justice, and ensuring a sound and progressive legal framework for Singaporeans. What the role is Under LPG, officers at the Civil & Legislative Policy Division (CLPD) do not just review laws — we play an important role in helping to shape the future of legal policy and governance in Singapore. Our team has driven reforms that touch the lives of Singaporeans every day. Some recent initiatives include: • Relief for victims of harassment: In 2021, we established the Protection from Harassment Court to give victims of harassment faster, more accessible and affordable relief through simplified court processes. • Modernisation of laws: In 2023, we modernised our laws through legislative reforms that make it possible for statutory declarations, oaths, affirmations, and notarisations to be done through electronic means. • Strengthening family therapeutic justice: The Maintenance Enforcement Process (MEP) was introduced in May 2023 under the Family Justice Reform Act to improve the enforcement of maintenance orders, deter non-payment, and improve access to justice for maintenance applicants through efficient enforcement procedures and sustainable outcomes. In 2025, the Maintenance Enforcement Division was established within the Insolvency and Public Trustee's Office to administer the MEP, with Maintenance Enforcement Officers working to achieve these objectives. • Enhancing the management of community disputes: In 2024, we worked closely with the MND and MCCY on enhancements to our Community Disputes Management Framework. The enhancements strengthen our community mediation framework and court processes to address neighbour disputes. Government agencies also worked together to introduce a Community Relations Unit that has powers to intervene in and address serious neighbour disputes. • Safer online spaces for Singaporeans: In November 2025, MinLaw and MDDI passed the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act. The Act strengthens online safety and protects Singaporeans from online harms. It empowers victims to seek timely relief and obtain redress through a new Online Safety Commission, and through new statutory torts that provide clear legal basis for victims of online harms to take action against those responsible for such harms. We are a small, multidisciplinary team that values thoughtful debate, moves with gumption, and is unafraid of breaking the mould. Officers will have the space to challenge assumptions and propose new ideas. This role is ideal for someone who is passionate about making a difference, thrives on intellectual challenge, and enjoys working collaboratively in a dynamic environment — and who wants their work to have tangible, national-level impact. You will join us in a variety of ongoing and upcoming policy reviews and reforms for the policy areas set out below: • Lead legal reform: Work with fellow officers to review laws, propose reforms and pursue new initiatives, tackling both classic and frontier issues. These include civil, family, and community justice issues, access to justice, criminal law and procedure, and more. jobs.title: (Senior) Assistant Director/ Infrastructure (Regulatory Excellence)
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 22 Sep 2026. Closing on 18 Oct 2026. The Built Environment (BE) sector is integral to the design, construction and maintenance of Singapore’s cityscape and infrastructure. However, the sector will need to confront the existential challenges of global climate change, energy and manpower constraints, changing demographics and values, and ageing infrastructure in the coming years. Addressing these challenges requires the ability to manage the trade-offs between the desired outcomes of greater safety, resiliency, quality, sustainability, liveability and as well as to strike a balance between industry regulation and development/promotion. You will be part of a passionate policy team in MND’s Infrastructure Division which serves as an advocate for businesses within the Built Environment (BE) sector, seeking and acting on suggestions on how rules and regulations imposed on the industry can be improved, saving businesses time, effort and money, while creating a nimble, forward looking and agile regulatory regime. You will champion regulatory innovation by steering rules review efforts across the BE sector. This includes staffing our Political Office Holders for the Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) on Pro-Enterprise Rules Review which reviews cross-cutting regulatory issues across the Whole-of-Government and reduces compliance burden for businesses. You will also support regulatory reviews to improve productivity across the BE sector, including through the Action Team to Improve Built Environment Productivity chaired by the Minister for National Development. This will involve working with agencies and industry stakeholders to identify regulatory, process and implementation issues that may affect productivity, and propose practical measures to streamline requirements, strengthen coordination and support sector-wide transformation. Further, you will lead the transformation of the sector through various initiatives, including encouraging digitalisation and adoption of regulatory technologies across the sector. In your capacity as Secretariat for the BE Rules Review Panel (RRP) chaired by PS/ND, you will work across 11 public agencies that perform regulatory functions in the BE sector. You will also serve as the deskhead for the Professional Engineers Board, giving you direct exposure to professional development and sector governance. Through your work, you will have the exciting opportunity to translate strategic intent and objectives to policy moves and programmes, and work closely with ministries and agencies across the Whole-of-Government. Depending on your level of seniority and experience, you may be given the opportunity to lead a small team. • A team player who fits into our division’s vibrant environment, and who can strengthen relationships with our agencies • Experience in regulatory policy development and/or operationalisation would be looked upon favourably • A strong command of English, both written and spoken • Strong interpersonal, analytical and problem-solving skills • A sense of initiative and dynamism • Attention to detail

jobs.title: Senior/Assistant Director, Supply Chain and Economic Resilience Division
jobs.inst: Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 5 Jun 2026. Closing on 30 Nov 2026. With the shifts in the global order and deepening geopolitical tensions, we live in a world which is less predictable and secure. In recent years, global supply chains are increasingly being scrutinised for their ability to withstand shocks. Countries are reconfiguring trade networks and supply chains in the name of resilience and security. As a small and open economy with limited natural resources, Singapore needs to be prepared and reacts nimbly in the face of such changes . The Supply Chain and Economic Resilience Division (SCERD) is responsible for ensuring economic resilience and the resilience of Singapore’s critical supply chains. SCERD also oversees building and institutionalising resilience, operational preparedness and crisis management capabilities in the Ministry of Trade and Industry. In this role, you will: • Develop national and sectoral strategies to secure the resilience of Singapore’s supply chains for essential and critical goods and services, and to mitigate and withstand impact from external shocks; • Analyse and synthesize findings on critical sector supply chains, challenges and needs; • Build the division’s collaboration network with key stakeholders across the Government, industry and academia; • Strengthen supply chain intelligence and analysis capabilities. jobs.title: Senior/Assistant Director, Low-Carbon Energy Division
jobs.inst: Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 9 Jul 2026. Closing on 31 Oct 2026. Energy security is an existential issue for Singapore. With the growing climate imperative, a global energy transition shifting to low-carbon fuels is underway. At the same time, geopolitical pressures are causing significant stresses in energy markets, leading to risks of supply disruptions and significant price volatility. The energy transition will be especially challenging for Singapore, given our scarce natural resources and limited renewable energy options. One of Singapore’s biggest challenges over the next few decades is to secure a low-carbon energy supply that is reliable and cost-competitive. The future of Singapore’s energy landscape depends on our ability to harness four switches – natural gas, solar, electricity imports, and low-carbon solutions such as hydrogen, ammonia and carbon capture and storage. METI’s Energy and Carbon (E&C) Cluster leads initiatives to reduce emissions and drive the transition to a low-carbon economy, while ensuring energy security and cost-competitiveness, and enabling Singapore to sustain economic growth. jobs.title: Assistant Director/Senior Assistant Director (Family Policy), FCD/FEC
jobs.inst: Ministry Of Social And Family Development
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 24 Jul 2026. The Family & Early Childhood (FEC) division sits under the Family and Child Development (FCD) Policy Directorate. The FEC division formulates and reviews policies that promote and strengthen families, in support of MSF’s macro outcomes to support marriage and parenthood actualisation and build strong and resilient marriages and families. Families are the bedrock of Singapore society. As Assistant Director (Family Policy), you will shape the policies and strategies that help Singaporeans build strong, resilient families — from supporting marriage and parenthood to ensuring that every child gets a good start in life, and that families are supported to care for elderly members with dignity. You will lead a team of policy officers across three broad areas of work. Strengthening Family Ties and Support Structures You will review and develop policies that promote strong family relationships across all life stages, with a particular focus on ensuring that elderly persons are well-supported by their families as they age. This includes identifying gaps in existing frameworks and working with MSF's Family Life Group (FLG) to translate policies into effective programmes and services on the ground. Strengthening Safeguards for Vulnerable Persons You will lead the review of the Mental Capacity Act and related policies, including those governing professional donees and deputyship, to ensure the legislative framework keeps pace with evolving needs and adequately protects persons who lack mental capacity. You will also drive efforts to encourage Singaporeans, especially the elderly, to plan ahead through instruments such as the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), reviewing policies and strategies to improve awareness and uptake. Funding and Legislative Review You will review MSF's funding approach for family services to ensure support is well-directed and fiscally sustainable, and lead reviews of key legislation including the Women's Charter, Mental Capacity Act, and Child Development Co-Savings Act to keep them aligned with policy objectives. Throughout all of this, you will work closely with FLG, NPTD and other stakeholders to implement, monitor, and continuously refine your policies based on evidence and ground feedback. • Good analytical, written and communication skills • Ability to propose and build support for evidence-based policies and solutions to address multi-faceted issues and perspectives • Good interpersonal and stakeholder management skills • Proactive in working with stakeholders to translate policies and solutions into implementation and monitor results for improvement • Prior supervisory experience and/or demonstrate leadership potential to lead a team and coach officers Only shortlisted candidates will be notified within 4 weeks from the closing date of this position.

jobs.title: Asst Director/Snr Asst Director/Deputy Director (Medical Service Scheme)
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 5 Aug 2026. Closing on 31 Dec 2026. Shape Singapore’s Health at the National Level Are you a medical doctor looking to make an impact beyond a clinical setting? Whether you are a junior doctor exploring your career options, or an established clinician contemplating new challenges to contribute at the national level, consider a career at the Ministry of Health (MOH). Under the MOH Medical Service Scheme employment, you will bring your clinical lens and expertise to national healthcare policies and influence decisions that shape the health of Singapore. You will work at the intersection of medicine and policy to design the healthcare systems and frameworks that aim to improve the health outcomes for the nation, and be part of the national health leadership. You will be working in a fast-paced environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time. This is a role for doctors who are energised by complexity, motivated by purpose, and ready to drive healthcare transformation at a national scale. You will contribute across four key domain areas: • Healthcare Regulation — Safeguarding standards and ensuring the safety, quality, and integrity of Singapore's healthcare system. • Manpower Development & Capability Building — Shaping the pipeline and professional development of Singapore's healthcare workforce. • Population Health & Health Services — Designing and delivering health programmes and services that keep Singaporeans healthy across their life course. • Quality, Value & Informatics — Driving innovation, data-driven decision making, and value in healthcare delivery. At more senior levels, you may also lead and manage a team. As part of your development, you may also be rotated to other public sector agencies and organisations within the broader healthcare ecosystem — such as the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), Health Promotion Board (HPB), Communicable Diseases Agency (CDA), or the public healthcare clusters. Your postings will be carefully designed to broaden your exposure and deepen your understanding of how policy translates into operations on the ground, equipping you with a well-rounded perspective to grow and contribute meaningfully throughout your career with MOH. While you will mostly be involved in healthcare policy work, you may also continue with sessional clinical practice, if you prefer, at the public healthcare institutions, so that you can maintain your clinical currency and familiarity with ground operations. We welcome applications from medical doctors who are registered with the Singapore Medical Council (SMC) and remain in good standing. Beyond your medical qualifications, we are looking for doctors who embody the following: • Collaborative Spirit: You work effectively in multidisciplinary teams and are energised by cross-agency initiatives that drive system-wide change. • Critical Thinking: You bring your medical perspectives to bear on complex policy questions, evaluating evidence rigorously to inform national healthcare decisions. • Capacity for Change: You are adaptable and responsive to evolving health priorities, emerging challenges, and shifting policy landscapes. • Commitment to Continuous Learning: You are passionate about growing beyond clinical practice — into the domains of healthcare policy, regulation, and population health strategy. • Compassion: You connect with diverse stakeholders with empathy, and understand how policy decisions translate into real outcomes for real people. We are also looking for doctors who demonstrate strength in systems thinking — the ability to understand complex healthcare ecosystems as a whole— as well as strategic thinking and the leadership capacity to inspire and guide teams through transformation. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, applicants may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

From supporting medium- to long-term strategic planning to navigating emerging risks, you will help translate issues and trade-offs into clear insights for senior decision-making, while building strong foundations in strategy, problem-solving, and stakeholder engagement early in your career. This is a unique opportunity to gain exposure to how strategic issues are framed, discussed and progressed at the senior leadership level, across a wide range of challenges spanning housing, land use, urban development, municipal services, technological change, risk and resilience, while building strong foundations in strategy, stakeholder management, and enterprise risk governance. - Shape strategic priorities and decision-making Support the development and refinement of the MND Family’s medium- to long-term priorities (5–10 years) by structuring issues, synthesising perspectives, and translating strategic considerations into clear papers and discussions. - Drive cross-cutting strategy projects Lead and structure blue sky initiatives that cut across divisions and agencies - bringing together different perspectives to tackle current and emerging system-level challenges, such as public service experience in an AI-driven society. - Shape senior leadership platforms Help design and drive key forums (e.g. senior management retreats and strategic discussions), ensuring that conversations are focused on the most critical issues and lead to clear outcomes. - Strengthen organisational resilience Identify emerging risks and vulnerabilities, and work with stakeholders to develop strategies that enhance the MND Family’s ability to respond to a rapidly changing environment. - Track what matters Develop and refine ways to monitor progress on key priorities, ensuring leadership has a clear, honest view of where things stand - and where course corrections are needed. Through policy and scheme governance and infrastructure projects with the industry, you will help anchor Singapore's position as a global payments hub. You will work at the centre of Singapore's national payments policy, scheme governance, and infrastructure — shaping how Singapore pays locally and across borders: Shape the rules and architecture of Singapore's national payment schemes — You will work on the establishment of Singapore Payments Network (SPaN), the single entity consolidating the governance and administration of schemes such as PayNow, FAST and SGQR. This includes developing risk and governance frameworks and refining scheme rules. In practice, this means consulting key stakeholders such as industry working groups, banks and payment service providers, and translating policy intent into operational scheme requirements that the ecosystem can implement. Contribute to a significant chapter in Singapore's payments evolution — The PayNow Generation 2 project is exploring enhancements that will improve how consumers, merchants, businesses, and government agencies pay and receive payments. You will work on initiatives spanning PayNow-NETS QR interoperability, deep-linking within PayNow QR codes for smoother online checkout, larger-value public sector PayNow transactions, and expanded payment capabilities such as request-to-pay, structured data fields for automated reconciliation, and a micropayments rail. Help shape Singapore's approach to the future of payments — AI-driven commerce is beginning to reshape how payments are initiated globally. Singapore is taking a deliberate approach to this shift: laying the groundwork for these capabilities while putting the right governance, consumer safeguards, and scheme rules in place first. You will contribute to frameworks, scheme rule amendments and pilot designs to explore how Singapore's national payment rails can best harness agentic payments. jobs.jd: Posting Date: 23 Sep 2026. Closing in 6 day(s). The Radiation Protection and Nuclear Science Group in the National Environment Agency (NEA) is the national authority for radiation protection in Singapore and serves to protect the public, radiation workers and the environment from the harmful effects of radiation. Its Nuclear Safety Division is responsible for developing capabilities, plans and ecosystems to support national nuclear safety & security assessment, radiological emergency response, and nuclear regulatory development efforts. The division is also responsible for ensuring that Singapore fulfils its obligations to international conventions and agreements with respect to the safe and peaceful use of nuclear material and technology. Singapore is studying the potential deployment of nuclear energy as part of its long-term energy strategy. Singapore will also need to prepare for the possibility of nuclear power deployment by other countries in the region. These endeavours involve conducting comprehensive studies and developing technical capabilities with respect to nuclear safety, security and safeguards (3S). You will be a key member of the team that will play a pivotal role in developing core capabilities necessary to (i) assess the safety and security performance of advanced nuclear energy technologies, (ii) develop drawer plans for 3S requirements, standards and acceptance criteria for a potential nuclear power programme, and (iii) ensure that Singapore adheres to international nuclear 3S obligations. This is a rare opportunity to be at the forefront of Singapore’s nuclear energy journey. Nuclear is a complex and emotive topic, and requires a diverse range of expertise to fully assess its implications for Singapore. By joining this team, you will have the opportunity to shape Singapore’s nuclear regulatory landscape, collaborate with international experts, and contribute to nuclear safety, security, safeguards and radiation protection capability building efforts domestically and regionally. Security . Develop technical requirements with respect to the security of nuclear materials and installations; and fulfil existing international security obligations. Assess and advance Singapore’s nuclear security-related interests at international, regional (including ASEAN) and bilateral platforms. Safeguards . Develop drawer plans, processes and tools for safeguards enhancements, including building capabilities in safeguards inspections and accountancy; and fulfil existing international safeguards obligations. Play a part in Singapore’s vision to build a Smart Nation and embark on your meaningful journey to build tech for public good. Join us to advance our mission and shape your future with us today! Learn more about GovTech at tech.gov.sg. The challenge What happens when technology, delivery and threats move faster than an organisation’s ability to see and respond to risk? And what could become possible if risk management moved just as quickly? Every organisation needs a way to detect warning signs, connect the dots and act before problems spread. That is the role of governance, risk and control. Think of it as the organisation’s nervous system. It picks up signals from across the organisation, helps leaders make sense of them and enables a timely response. When that system works well, teams can move faster, take smarter risks and deliver with greater confidence. When it does not, warning signs are missed, decisions slow down and governance becomes a barrier rather than an enabler. GovTech has strong platforms, talented people and an important mission. As our role and public impact grow, the risks we manage are becoming more interconnected, fast-moving and consequential. We are looking for Deputy Directors and Assistant Directors in Enterprise Risk Management who want to help build what comes next. You will have the opportunity to challenge established practices, experiment with data and AI, influence senior decisions and shape how one of Singapore’s most important technology organisations manages risk. [What you will be working on] This is a role for people who want more than a steady portfolio. It is for those who want to build, push boundaries and leave the system better than they found it. What you will have the chance to change. We want to move enterprise risk management: from periodic reporting to more continuous risk visibility from manual collation to data and AI-enabled insight from risk registers to clearer decisions and action from unclear accountability to risks with active owners from retrospective assurance to earlier intervention from compliance activity to practical support for delivery This is not simply a reporting role. You will help shape how risk is understood, discussed, owned and acted upon across GovTech. Your mandate Your job is to make enterprise risk management useful. You will work with senior leaders, risk owners and teams across GovTech to identify what matters, make trade-offs visible and support action before issues become incidents. Depending on your experience and appointment level, you will lead or take ownership of significant ERM portfolios and initiatives. You will have room to test ideas, challenge established practices and build better approaches. You will also need to influence people you do not manage and create clarity where risks, priorities or accountabilities are contested. That is part of the job. Break the Frame Modern risk management cannot rely only on inherited frameworks, templates and periodic reporting. We want people who are prepared to question established practices, test better approaches and rethink how risk management should work in a technology organisation. Key Responsibilities High-Concurrency Operational Management Directly manage multiple offensive teams executing simultaneous, distinct victim operations across separate target networks or business entities. De-conflict operational resources, timelines, and personnel to ensure high-fidelity, continuous testing across multiple concurrent environments. Handle the inherent ambiguity of shifting variables across multiple live runs, ensuring every operation maintains rigid operational security (OPSEC). C2 Architecture & Advanced Malware Development Oversee the design, deployment, and operational management of complex Command and Control (C2) frameworks capable of supporting multi-tenant, simultaneous operations. Enforce best practices in C2 server segregation, obfuscation, and traffic routing to prevent defensive detection across various target environments. Ensure that simultaneous red team campaigns realistically mimic the specific Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs) of modern Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) targeting the respective victims. Stakeholder Interface & Operational Coordination Act as the primary interface for all affected stakeholders, providing regular, precise updates on active exploitation paths and findings during live runs. Coordinate complex, multi-stakeholder rating exercises, ensuring seamless collaboration and communication before, during, and after a specific operational run. Learn more about GovTech at tech.gov.sg. [What you will be working on] Some problems are easy to walk past. Others keep nagging at you. Why are we still doing this manually? Why does sensible policy become painful when it meets the real world? Why do we discover risks after the fact when the signals were already there? How should government govern AI systems that increasingly make decisions and take actions for themselves? And why, when technology can change in minutes, does governance sometimes still move in months? If questions like these bother you enough that you want to get underneath them, experiment with better answers and solve the real-world problem, we should talk. We are rethinking what modern governance, risk and assurance could look like across GovTech and, ultimately, the wider Singapore Government. GovTech is where we can design, build, test and learn. The ambition is bigger. Why this matters We are modernising Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) so government can use technology and AI with greater confidence, improve services faster, and keep the essential systems people rely on dependable and resilient. Ultimately, the test is bigger than GRC: Can government use technology better, serve citizens better, and retain their trust when things go wrong? That is the problem behind this role. And we do not expect to solve it by designing the perfect framework in a room. We expect to work on real systems, with real users and real constraints. To experiment. Test assumptions. Prototype, understand behavior and incentives. Learn from what does not work. And turn what does into something that can work at government scale. One role. Multiple archetypes. You might begin with strength in one. Over time, you can acquire additional archetypes without giving up the ones you already have. An engineer might combine GRC Platform Engineering with Policy Engineering and AI Governance. An assurance practitioner might bring together Threat-Informed Risk Intelligence, Enterprise Risk Management and Systems Architecture. Some practitioners will build deep expertise in one or two. Others will develop a broader combination across several. Neither is a prescribed progression. The archetypes are not boxes to move between. They are capabilities you can accumulate, combine and apply. As the Responsible AI & Governance Manager, you will help shape how GovTech governs AI adoption across the organisation. You will develop practical governance frameworks, operationalise AI policies, and partner with teams to ensure AI solutions are developed and deployed responsibly while enabling innovation. Rather than acting as a compliance gatekeeper, you will work closely with delivery teams to embed governance into the way AI products and services are designed, built and operated. Design governance artefacts, assessment methodologies and operational processes. Support teams in adopting responsible AI practices throughout the product lifecycle. Support governance reviews of higher-risk and higher-impact AI use cases. Develop governance playbooks, templates and operating procedures. Promote risk-based governance approaches that enable safe experimentation and innovation. AI Risk Management Identify emerging risks arising from AI technologies and adoption patterns. Track remediation actions and implementation of governance recommendations. Monitor governance effectiveness and propose improvements where necessary.
